artworks.title: The Abduction of Europa
artworks.description: Rembrandt's Europa on the bull — the princess Asterius of Crete will marry after Zeus leaves her, raising Minos, Rhadamanthys and Sarpedon as his foster-sons.

artworks.title: The Rape of Europa
artworks.description: Titian's poesie: Europa carried to Crete — the island where Asterius (Asterion) becomes her mortal husband and the boys' foster-father. Not Asterius the Minotaur, nor the Thessalian Argonaut.

popCulture.title: Asterion (king of Crete)
popCulture.description: Cretan prince who marries Europa and raises Zeus' sons — carefully distinct from Asterius/Asterion as a name of the Minotaur.

popCulture.title: Europa (consort of Zeus)
popCulture.description: Asterius' wife after the bull-ride — mother of Minos, Rhadamanthys and Sarpedon in the house he fosters.

popCulture.title: Minos
popCulture.description: Asterius' most famous foster-son — the Cretan lawgiver whose mortal stepfather holds the throne until the boys quarrel and leave.
